title: Like the Wind
text: A revolution is unfolding within Melromarc. The revolutionary forces form a long, snaking line. From far off, we watch as they march toward Melromarc Castle. Things have changed quite a bit in just a single week.
“Hey, Motoyasu, things have turned out quite differently from what you predicted…”
Since we’ve already come this far, there’s no helping it—we’re using the portal to Siltvelt without hiding it.
“That’s strange. In the future, things didn’t get this chaotic. Sure, there were citizens who were cooperative with my Father, but…”
“Could this be… because we did too many good deeds?”
“But I’ve only heard good things about my Father in the future, too.”
“Maybe there was a problem with how we handled it. If they were short on money, maybe we charged high prices when selling goods… or maybe we didn’t go that far with food rations.”
“Would that really make a difference?”

“Absolutely. There’s a big difference in the sense of gratitude between someone who does a good deed but then extorts money in return, and someone who does it for free! Well… we were careful to make sure it didn’t become taken for granted.”

If you show goodwill every time, the recipient starts to take it for granted. Father was careful about that, too. If that’s the case, the difference between this incident and the first world is that we did too many good deeds. It feels like everyone is so eager to expose the country’s conspiracy that they’re putting all their faith in my Father.
“For now, it’d probably be best to talk things over with everyone in Siltvelt. The way things are… even the queen can’t come here without risking trouble.”
“Oh? Wouldn’t things be resolved if the queen returned?”

“If you can think that after seeing what happened, you’re really something. Sure, Melty-chan and the Queen might be welcomed. But… hmm, am I overthinking this? Anyway, if I were the Queen, I couldn’t go back to the country in a state like this.”
“And why is that?”

“The Queen wants to mediate between me—the Shield Hero—and her country for the sake of friendship; she doesn’t want to throw her own country into chaos. Melromarc is currently in a state where the Three Heroes Church and the revolutionaries are all mixed together. Right now, it’s just a standoff and small-scale skirmishes, but if the Queen were to return home at this point, the balance of power would tip way too far.”
“I’m sure it’ll work out somehow. Que sera, sera.”
He’s treating this like it’s none of his business. I try to reassure my Father that he’s overthinking it, but his expression doesn’t brighten up.
“Rather… the king’s authority seems to be fading too much…”
Father has been deep in thought the whole time. Has something gone wrong?

“For now, let’s focus on the waves. Tomorrow is the Melromarc wave, right? If the Three Heroes Church is planning to target us, it’ll surely happen then. After all, they probably think we’re hiding out in Melromarc.”
“Then we shouldn’t participate. If we just let them keep thinking you’re in hiding, the revolutionaries will crush them in no time.”
Well, they do have powerful weapons, but once they start causing trouble, we’ll just have to reveal ourselves and take them down—and that’ll be the end of it.
“That’s true… Motoyasu, was there anything dangerous during the next wave? As long as nothing key happened, it shouldn’t be a problem.”
When my Father asked me that, I recalled the second wave. I’m pretty sure the boss was a Soul Eater. After that, a pig with a translucent fan appeared…
“Everyone except you, Father, lost to the second boss that emerged from the wave.”
“W-Wow, you managed to survive that.”
“I heard Father put up a good fight and forced the enemy to retreat. When I first heard it, I scoffed and thought it was impossible.”
“…Wait, if we stay silent, the only one participating in the wave is Itsuki—doesn’t that mean Itsuki will lose and die!?”

Huh! Now that you mention it, that’s right! For the same reason, even if Ren were to participate in the wave, they’d lose without us. In other words, if we don’t intervene here, the loop is guaranteed. Since this is so important, we have to keep it in mind even if we do end up in a loop.
“So, what should we do?”
“We’ve got no choice! We’d better rush to where the Wave is happening, right? Fortunately, Motoyasu-kun has knowledge of the future, so he might be the one to go.”
“But according to what we just discussed, isn’t the Three Heroes Church supposed to send assassins to the site of the Wave?”

“If Itsuki is acting as Motoyasu-kun knows he would, they shouldn’t be organized into a formation. Probably, the assassins will be Itsuki and his group. They’ll likely claim it’s under the pretext of kidnapping Melty-chan and brainwashing the citizens.”
“Then I’ll quickly put an end to the wave and withdraw. You, Father, should just take it easy over in Siltvelt.”
Nah, from where I stand now, any enemy is just small fry. I haven’t been fighting much lately, so my body’s actually gotten a bit rusty.
“In that case… yeah. Motoyasu-kun is very strong, so you might be able to repel the assassins—Itsuki and his group—while quelling the Wave. Can I leave it to you?”
“Leave it to me! I’ll handle it!”
And so, I accepted Father’s request and decided to quell the Wave separately from him.
The next day. I’m waiting at the spot where the waves are expected to occur, along with Yuki-chan and Kou.
“The waves are about to start, right?”
“That’s right.”
“What should Kou and the others do?”
“Just run toward the crack in the waves before the monsters appear.”
“Is that so? That’s no fun.”
“Hahaha, the goal this time is to finish it quickly. Getting away afterward might be more of a hassle.”

You never know what might happen. Judging by the first run, I imagine Itsuki and his group will head straight for the crack in the wave as usual. According to Father, Itsuki will likely try to capture us. So, the plan was to wrap things up early and make sure Itsuki is safe.
Just as I was mentally rehearsing the strategy and visualizing future events, a crack appeared in the sky. It’s begun.
“Let’s go!”
“I’ll do it!”
“Dash!”
Yuki-chan starts running with me on her back, and Kou follows close behind. When I look around, sure enough, Itsuki’s group has appeared.
“Ah!”

Itsuki’s group is pointing at me, but I don’t even know who they are. We zoomed past them like the wind. They were saying something, but I couldn’t hear a thing. Those guys are totally just background characters.
“Yuki-chan! Faster! Keep pushing forward!”
“Here we go! High Quick!”
“Kou, too—”

Monsters are swarming out of the cracks in the waves—I’m pretty sure they’re shadow monsters of the Demi-Human type—and Soul Eaters are emerging from the waves right now. Yuki-chan and the others push their speed to the absolute limit, rushing toward the distant wave fissure as fast as they can. It would still take far too long on foot. But this time, there’s no holding back—we’re going all out.
“Liberation Firesquall X! Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X!”

The moment the monsters emerge from the wave, they unleash a wide-area rain of fire, wiping out the minions. It’s a hassle if they spread out, after all. Next, they use the area-of-effect attacks from the Aiming Lancer and Brionac to blow away the wave’s fissure along with the monsters.

Not only did they blow away the monsters and the Soul Eater, but the wave’s fissure closed in an instant. The damage was practically zero. At most, a massive rain of fire poured down on the spot where the wave fissure had been, turning it into a scorched wasteland. Since Father told me to “take care of this quickly,” the only downside—if you can call it that—is that I can’t recover the monsters’ corpses.
“Is it over already? I just ran over there, that’s all. Kitamura.”
“Hahaha, the point of a wave is to finish it quickly, you see.”
“That was a letdown. I’d like a more challenging battle, Motoyasu-sama.”
“You’ve gotten too strong. Maybe next time we should do some training exercises with my Father and the others?”
“That sounds like a good idea. That dragon has gotten quite powerful lately—it’s a real challenge to take down.”
Just as we were talking, an arrow flew in from behind us. I casually deflected the arrow and turned Yuki-chan around.
“I don’t know how you managed to quell the waves so quickly, but Motoyasu! I need to talk to you!”
“Oh my, what could you possibly want at this late hour? You’re so late I was about to yawn, Itsuki.”
There stood Itsuki and his party, staring at us with pure hostility.
